This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in prescribeObjectFormForArrayFilter))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in prescribeObjectFormForArrayFilter))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 17566664299edac816b6672a673ac82b192d24ea` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ea20c23e88f89142a7361728680fbfa72220250e` — the merge of head `f5eede77bb769a4c56ffd070c5a33f978a5b2788` into base `17566664299edac816b6672a673ac82b192d24ea`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ea20c23e88f89142a7361728680fbfa72220250e && git checkout ea20c23e88f89142a7361728680fbfa72220250e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 17566664299edac816b6672a673ac82b192d24ea f5eede77bb769a4c56ffd070c5a33f978a5b2788 && git checkout -B drift-repro 17566664299edac816b6672a673ac82b192d24ea && git merge --no-ff f5eede77bb769a4c56ffd070c5a33f978a5b2788

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 17566664299edac816b6672a673ac82b192d24ea
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 17566664299edac816b6672a673ac82b192d24ea` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f5eede77bb769a4c56ffd070c5a33f978a5b2788`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/analytics-carrier-filter.ts + packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/dataset.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/report.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/error-map.zod.ts, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json, packages/spec/scripts/lib/dropped-refinements.ts, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-doc-authoring.mjs, AGENTS.md

Inputs read: card #30124 (body, triage 6636116300, claim 6663650795, amendment 6663714630, os-dev-report 6664461198), PR #30599 (body, 3-file list, net diff `2ffdb649..f5eede77`), the head's check-runs at 2026-11-05T17:47Z. Remainder of the diff (`.changeset/30124-analytics-filter-array-refusal.md`, `packages/spec/src/data/filter-save-door-face-parity.test.ts` §8) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; read here only as cited code.

Gate verdicts on the head (check-run conclusions, the reading above): `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, the three scoped lints, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` (8/8 shards), `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check PR Size` — all `success`; the opt-in and docs families `skipped`. No family red.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set byte-identical — right.** `analyticsCarrierFilter()` (analytics-carrier-filter.ts:207-211) adds one `$ZodCheck` to the `.optional()` wrapper. Its body (L253-266) returns unless `Array.isArray(payload.value)` AND `payload.issues.length > 0`; it then rewrites one existing issue's `message` and splices out at most one sibling, and only after finding the record-arm issue it keeps. It never pushes an issue (no accepted value becomes refused) and never removes the last issue (the kept record issue stays, so no refused value becomes accepted). Non-array refusals are untouched. Read against `FilterConditionSchema` (filter.zod.ts:2332-2338): `z.record(...).and(z.object({...}))`, so an array fails both intersection arms with `invalid_type` at path `[]` (`expected: 'record'` and `expected: 'object'`); that is the exact pair the check matches on (`atSlot`, L256-259). The §8 battery (17 values, carrier verdict === bare `FilterConditionSchema.optional()` verdict, non-array issues `toEqual`) pins this.
- **Only the text changes — right.** The kept issue retains `code`, `expected`, `input`, `path`; a preset raw-issue `message` wins over the context error map, so the ObjectStack map's `Expected record but received object.` (error-map.zod.ts:106-119) no longer prints for this slot, while every other `invalid_type` in the tree keeps it. The test "the message is the same with no error map" pins that the words are the issue's own.
- **Published JSON Schema unchanged — right.** The check is a `custom` kind with no JSON form, attached to the same `ZodOptional` node that already carries the nested-relation `superRefine`. The dropped-refinement census records ONE site per node with a `count` field that the ledger does not store (dropped-refinements.ts:483-512; ledger carries `sites` paths only), and `ui/DashboardWidget`, `ui/Dataset`, `ui/DatasetMeasure`, `ui/Report`, `ui/JoinedReportBlock` already list `filter` / `measures.element.filter` / `runtimeFilter` / `blocks.element.runtimeFilter` (baseline L1650-1680, L1743-1748, L1941-1949). No generated artifact is in the diff, which is what "unchanged" must look like; `Spec property liveness` and `Type Check · source gates` are green on the head.
- **Public surface unchanged — right.** `ANALYTICS_FILTER_ARRAY_MESSAGE` is exported from `analytics-carrier-filter.ts`, which `packages/spec/src/ui/index.ts` does not re-export (grep: no hit; only `dashboard.zod` / `report.zod` / `dataset.zod` at L41-43). The test imports it by relative path. `import type { z }` becoming `import { z }` is a runtime import of a dependency the module already reached through `../data/filter.zod`.
- **All five carriers covered — right.** `dashboard.zod.ts:1182`, `dataset.zod.ts:421` and `:667`, `report.zod.ts:454` and `:602` all call `analyticsCarrierFilter()`; nothing else does (grep over `packages/spec/src` non-test files). The other `FilterConditionSchema` carriers (query `where`, L2394, etc.) are not touched.
- **Message bypasses the error map on purpose — right, and consistent with the tree.** Every hand-written refusal in `filter.zod.ts` / `view.zod.ts` is the issue's own text; this one joins them.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/30124-analytics-filter-array-refusal.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, body carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body carries the same two line-initial declarations. Read against AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 (L1019-1036): a bug fix in a released package takes `patch`, never `skip-changeset`; `none` takes `patch`. Read against `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` "The LEVEL axis" (L880-940): `none` must grade every introduced entry `patch` (it does, one entry), must not move an `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` baseline (none in the diff), and `added` beside `Clause-②: no` is not declared. The diff widens and narrows no accept set (① above), so `Clause-②: no` is the true reading and no `(narrowing)` arm or BREAKING banner is owed. The changeset body states the FROM/TO text and the "accepted before, accepted now" invariant, which is what the CHANGELOG reader needs. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. **Clause-②: no — holds.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — none to answer.
- Dev flag (PR Acceptance notes, and `out_of_scope_findings`): the error map's `invalid_type` branch prints `typeof input`, so any OTHER slot refusing an array still reads `received object`. Answered: correct reading of error-map.zod.ts:116; it is a tree-wide error-map property outside this card (the card asks for the widget filter's refusal to name the object form), and the PR does not touch it. Not escalated; the dev's note on the PR body is the right carrier. A follow-up card is the maintainer's call.
- Deviation "PR attribution second line links this card thread, not the seat thread": accepted — the harness writes its own thread link; the seat signature line below it names the seat and session, and the PR-body guards are green.
- Deviation "no PR assignee or reviewer": accepted — os-dev forbids them on a dev's `pr_create`; the seat assigns at hand-off.
- Deviation "commit trailers are the model-free pair": read on both branch commits (`0493b0477b`, `f5eede77bb`): `Claude-Session:` + `Co-authored-by: Claude`. Accepted; not a contract question.
- Card scope exclusion (triage 6636116300, claim `File surface`): unifying the view and widget filter shapes is out. Held — the diff changes no shape, only the words. `ui/**`, `skills/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md` untouched (3-file list).
- Docs Drift Check (6664463239) lists 6 pages via the `invalid_type` string literal in `prescribeObjectFormForArrayFilter`. That literal is a comparison against zod's issue code, not a new emitted code; no page under `content/docs`, `skills` or `docs` restates the old `Expected record but received object` text (grep: no hit). Nothing owed.
- Premise: `premise_still_valid: true`; the §8 comment records the two-issue measurement on `origin/main` `2ffdb649`, and `FilterConditionSchema`'s intersection on `main` produces exactly that pair. Holds.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ui/analytics-carrier-filter.ts`** — judged against `FilterConditionSchema` (filter.zod.ts:2332), the `view.zod.ts` mechanism it borrows (`reportClaimedFilterElementBranch` L1250-1268, `focusClaimedBranch` L7544-7580), the five carriers, the error map, and the card's scenario (a list view's rule array copied into a widget `filter`).

- **Mechanism holds.** `new z.core.$ZodCheck({ check: 'custom', when: () => true })` with `_zod.check` assigned is byte-for-byte the pattern `view.zod.ts` uses twice (L1251-1252, L7545-7546), whose docblock (L7519-7523) records why `when` is what lets a check see an aborted parse. The check is the last on the node, after the `superRefine` walk, which is skipped on an aborted array anyway; the order cannot interleave with the walk's issues because the walk only runs on a parse that did not abort.
- **Matching is tight enough.** `expected === 'record'` / `'object'` at path length 0 can only be this node's own intersection arms: a nested record/object failure carries a non-empty relative path, and the `.optional()` wrapper adds no issue of its own. If a future zod renamed the `expected` literal the check degrades to a no-op (returns at `recordIndex === -1`) and §8's five per-carrier pins go red — fail-loud, not fail-silent.
- **The prescription is true against the code it names.** `where` is `FilterConditionSchema.optional()` (filter.zod.ts:2394); `$in` is `setMembershipSchema` taking a list (L1868), `$gte` an ordering comparand (L1860); a bare value is implicit equality and sibling record keys AND (the `FilterCondition` type, L2231-2256); `$or` is `z.array(FilterConditionSchema)` (L2336). The "rule array a list view's `filter` takes" is `ViewFilterRuleSchema` `{ field, operator, value }` (view.zod.ts:1048-1075; `'in'` is in `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS`, L321) carried by `filter: z.array(ViewFilterElementSchema)` (L1997, L3376). The message names all five slots (widget `filter`, dataset's and measure's `filter`, report's `runtimeFilter`, which covers the joined block) and shows the fix for the card's exact repro.
- **No tracker id in a runtime string.** `ANALYTICS_FILTER_ARRAY_MESSAGE` (L221-228) carries none; `[#30124]` appears only in comments, the same convention as `[#20080]` / `[#20116]` already in this file. `check-doc-authoring` Rule 3 (L344+) walks message positions in `packages/spec/src/**`; `Lint · docs & code guards` is green on the head.
- **Tried to break it:** `undefined` (optional short-circuit, check sees `undefined`, returns), `null` / scalars (not arrays, untouched), `[]` and `[{}]` (both arrays, one issue each — pinned), an array nested under `$and` (the slot value is an object, so the check returns and the nested member's own pass refuses it with its own path), a widget inside a `$or` of dashboards (paths prefixed by the parent after the check ran, so the relative-path-0 test is unaffected). Nothing moved a verdict.
- **Residual, not a finding:** a scalar or `null` in the slot still earns the error map's twin pair (`Expected record but received string.` / `Expected object but received string.`), now redundant rather than contradictory. The card measured the array shape, the triage scoped it so, and widening the check to every non-object would need a second message; a follow-up card, if the maintainer wants it.

No must-fix. No should-fix.
